summary.headline: Schneider Electric Infrastructure Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 20% YoY to INR780 crore, but PAT fell 43% to INR30 crore on commodity-driven margin squeeze.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 orders reached about INR1,265 crore against INR900 crore in the prior quarter, and H1 orders grew about 25%, per management. Revenue rose about 20% YoY to around INR780 crore, with H1 revenue up about 12.5% to INR1,400 crore after a weak Q1 execution. EBIT margin recovered to 7.2% in Q2 from about 4% in Q1 (H1: 6.2%), but PAT fell to INR30 crore from INR52 crore as copper, transformer oil and steel costs rose faster than pricing could pass them through. Management did not guide on margins and said H2 leverage depends on revenue growth and commodity relief.

financial_highlights.change: up from about INR900 crore in the prior quarter (per analyst); H1 orders up about 25%
up sequentially from about 4% in Q1

segments.name: Medium voltage components (Kolkata)
segments.commentary: Management said Kolkata interrupter capacity is being raised from 1.8 lakh to 2.5 lakh and then to 3.75 lakh units per year; a fully digitalised, sensorised breaker started production in Kolkata. Three-pole MV breakers are made there.

segments.name: Emerging segments (data centres, semiconductors, renewables)
segments.commentary: Management cited a semiconductor powertrain order (switchgear and transformers) and a skid-mounted data centre substation in West India as wins; about 1.6 GW of data centres is operating, with 2.5-3 GW reported at financial close or under construction.

segments.name: Projects / ETO and standard products
segments.commentary: Projects are about 60-65% of business; only about 20-25% of project backlog carries price variation protection. Standard products are repriced, but customers take time to accept increases.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin guidance; management said margin dilution from commodities (copper, transformer oil, steel) is not coming down.
Management expects H2 operating leverage from higher revenue and possible easing of commodity prices.
Export mix is about 12-13% of revenue; management expects it to stay broadly similar as domestic and export markets both grow.
Kolkata capacity expansion approved by the Board last week; partial capitalisation has started, raising depreciation.
Management expects the RDSS scheme extended by two years; about INR18,000 crore of its outlay is cited for the current year.
capex_capacity: KMVC (Kolkata) capacity expansion approved by the Board last week; partial capitalisation started, raising depreciation.
Kolkata MV interrupter capacity: 85,000 pieces previously, expanding to 1.8-1.85 lakh, then 2.5 lakh and now 3.75 lakh units per year.
Phase II approval received for Kolkata; a shift of assets from the Salt Lake facility to the new site is planned for coming quarters.
Management said Kolkata has space for further expansion.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of INR1,265 crore was described as sustained, but management would not call it a one-off or a new run-rate; large-ticket orders were not present in Q2.
Management is becoming selective, avoiding contracts where commodity risk is high.
Price pass-through: quotes use current price indices plus contingency, but a commodity rise of more than 10% between booking and execution (quarter to quarter) was not fully recovered.
Tenders from PSUs often prohibit price variation clauses, so cost escalation can't be recovered on those contracts.
Data centre demand: about 1.6-1.7 GW operating in India, with management citing an 8 GW target by 2030 (6.5-8 GW range).

qa_highlights.question: What share of the backlog is legacy at old prices, and what share is protected by price variation clauses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the legacy figure. About 20-25% of the backlog is in projects, and roughly 20-25% of project backlog is protected by variation clauses. Around 20-25% of the order book shifts beyond one year.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q2 order inflow of INR1,265 crore driven by one-off large orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not call the quarter one-off, since large orders come in some quarters and not others. Demand is seen as sustained, but the chief executive said orders depend on the capex cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Is export mix about 12-15% of revenue, and what is the margin difference for exports?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said export mix is about 12-13%, which should stay similar as domestic also grows. Export pricing follows arm's-length transfer pricing, while domestic is L1-competitive; exports add operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Kolkata MV capacity raised twice within about three months?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said demand is the reason: capacity was raised from 85,000 pieces to about 1.8-1.85 lakh, then 2.5 lakh and now 3.75 lakh, to be future-ready for global demand.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins recover, and does the cost escalation clause apply?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO gave no guidance. Ex-commodity material margins are on track, but commodity inflation (copper, transformer oil, steel) keeps rising. Escalation clauses exist but are often not enforceable in tenders.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from copper, transformer oil and steel, with incomplete pass-through on fixed-price PSU tenders.
PAT down 43% YoY; H2 operating leverage needs revenue growth to materialise.
Order inflow lumpiness: management does not treat Q2's INR1,265 crore as a run-rate.
Rupee depreciation and a less supportive interest rate environment, which management flagged.
Finance cost increase from the higher rate paid (6.1% to 6.7%); depreciation rising as KMVC capitalises.
Monitor the Kolkata asset relocation timing against customer commitments, and whether the 3.75 lakh unit expansion is absorbed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and long-term data centre and renewables opportunities, but noticeably cautious and defensive on margins. Management avoided margin guidance and said commodity pressure is not easing.
key_quotes: We are becoming a bit choosy and perhaps not taking an exposure where we see larger risk.
What I was saying that about 1.6 gigawatt is already up and running.
We are pretty confident that this breaker, which is being produced in your plant in Kolkata, will actually drive the trend.
So that's the only reason, but just rest assured that the current costing, the tendering we do, always the latest price we do.
